title: Result type alias absent from 7 substantive crates
description:
7 crates define a pub type Result<T> = core::result::Result<T, Error> alias (pkix-path, pkix-revocation, pkix-chain, pkix-chain-simple, pkix-path-builder, pkix-ct, pkix-ac). The remaining crates with public Error types do NOT: pkix-truststore, pkix-identity, pkix-aia, pkix-lint, pkix-zlint-bridge, pkix-revocation-http, pkix-profiles, pkix-profiles-cabf, pkix-lint-cabf.

The missing aliases are inconsistent with the crates that have them. For crates that define their own Error enum and return Result<_, Error> from public functions, having the alias is the workspace convention. Not having it means callers write pkix_truststore::Result<Vec<TrustAnchor>> vs the verbose core::result::Result<Vec<TrustAnchor>, pkix_truststore::Error>.

Notably pkix-truststore and pkix-identity both have public Error types and multiple public functions returning Result<_, Error>, yet neither defines the alias. pkix-revocation-http has three different error types (ExtractError, FetchError, and no unified Error), so missing the alias is understandable there.

Impact: minor ergonomic inconsistency. Callers importing from crates that happen to have the alias can write pkix_path::Result<T>, but cannot do the same for pkix_truststore or pkix_identity. Not a functional issue but a naming convention gap.

Crates that should gain the alias: pkix-truststore, pkix-identity.
